chunks: Or do you ask of them any tribute? In that case the tribute of your Lord is better, for He is the best of providers.
ai.seo_question: What compensation did the Prophet ask for according to this verse?
ai.summary: In the context of the Meccan period, this verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) that his mission is divinely funded, negating the need for worldly tribute often demanded by contemporary leaders. Shia exegetes highlight that 'khuraj' (tribute) refers to the specific payment given to prophets, emphasizing that Allah’s provision is superior to any material compensation, thereby affirming the Prophet’s spiritual independence and reliance on the Best of Providers.
